channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Australia GDP misses expectations: What 0.3% growth means for AUD/USD
item.description: Australia’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) rose 0.3% QoQ in the first quarter (Q1) of 2026 compared with the 0.8% growth in the fourth quarter of 2025, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) showed on Wednesday. This reading came in weaker than the expectations of 0.5% expansion.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8184 vs. 6.8187 previous
item.description: On Wednesday, the People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead at 6.8184 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8187 and 6.7673 Reuters estimate.

item.title: WTI rises to near $93.00 as Iran launches missiles toward Kuwait, Bahrain
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) gains ground for the third successive day, trading around $92.90 per barrel during the Asian hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen struggles near 160.00 threshold vs USD; bears shrug off intervention warning
item.description: The USD/JPY pair touches a fresh one-month high during the Asian session on Wednesday, though it struggles to build on the momentum beyond the 160.00 psychological mark. The fundamental backdrop, however, favors bulls and suggests that the path of least resistance for spot prices is to the upside.

item.title: US forces conduct strikes after Iran's attack
item.description: The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) said on Tuesday that it had intercepted and defeated a series of Iranian missile and drone attacks targeting regional neighbors, including Kuwait and Bahrain, while also carrying out self-defence strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, ABC News reported.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama: Ready to act on forex if required
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Wednesday that the authorities are ready to act on the foreign exchange if required.

item.title: Gold declines to near $4,450 amid fading Iran peace hopes
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) tumbles to around $4,465 during the early Asian session on Wednesday. The precious metal extends the decline amid uncertainty surrounding the peace deal between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Uptrend holds, eyes on 216.00, BoJ risks loom
item.description: The Pound Sterling advances versus the Japanese Yen on Tuesday, up by 0.24%, driven by traders’ optimism about a US-Iran deal, even though there are rumours that Iran has halted negotiations amid the Israel-Hezbollah conflict over the weekend.

item.title: Australia’s S&P Global Services PMI beats estimates: Here's what it means for AUD/USD
item.description: The final reading of Australia's S&P Global Services PMI came in at 48.7 in May, compared to 50.7 in the previous reading, the latest data published by S&P Global showed on Wednesday. This figure came in better than the estimates of 47.7.

item.title: China: Slower 2Q26 growth outlook – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Ho Woei Chen notes that China’s May PMIs point to softer 2Q26 GDP growth, with manufacturing hovering at the expansion threshold and services rebounding only modestly.

item.title: MENA FX: Carry unwinds pressure regional currencies – BNY
item.description: BNY's Bob Savage notes that most MENA (Middle East and North Africa) currencies saw net selling in May after a brief April respite, with fixed income also underperforming.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar pressured by strong US labor-market data
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades near the 0.5930 region on Wednesday as the United States (US) Dollar (USD) strengthens following upbeat labor-market data, while investors remain cautious ahead of upcoming economic releases from New Zealand. At the time of writing, the pair declines around 0.15%.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Mild upside with 6.7500 in focus against dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that USD/CNH was little changed on Monday around 6.7652, but the underlying tone has softened. They expect the pair to drift lower intraday within 6.7595–6.7690 rather than stage a sharp decline.

item.title: Euro stalls as Oil shock keeps the US Dollar in play
item.description: The Euro (EUR) consolidates within familiar levels on Tuesday, flatlining around 1.1630 as the US Dollar (USD) recovers some ground, underpinned by high Oil prices amid halted US-Iran talks, even though US President Donald Trump says this is fake news.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Forecasts cut on tougher backdrop – OCBC
item.description: OCBC's strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong lower their Indonesian Rupiah (IDR) forecasts despite Bank Indonesia’s (BI) larger-than-expected 50 bp hike, arguing that renewed domestic policy uncertainty and an unfavourable external backdrop are weighing on IDR.

item.title: Philippine Peso: Year-end 2026 forecast raised to 62.7 against US Dollar – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee at DBS Group Research has raised his USD/PHP year-end 2026 forecast to 62.7 from 57.8, reflecting persistent external and domestic pressures. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz and higher Oil prices have widened trade deficits and pushed inflation well above target.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar gains on strong JOLTS data, traders await key labor market reports
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) strengthened near the 99.20 price zone after the latest JOLTS Job Openings report surged to 7.618 million in April from 6.887 million in March, well above market expectations of 6.88 million.

item.title: Australian Dollar's resilience is imported from China
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is sitting near the top of the major currency leaderboard, adding close to 0.3% on the day and pushing back toward 0.7200 after defending 0.7150. Almost none of that strength is homegrown.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Global usage trends higher in 2026 – Standard Chartered
item.description: Standard Chartered’s Tommy Wu reports that the bank’s revamped Renminbi Globalisation Index shows higher global RMB usage in February–April 2026 versus late 2025.

item.title: South Korean Won: AI support versus Hormuz risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Michael Wan argues that strong AI-related demand and semiconductor exports are offsetting Strait of Hormuz spillovers for some Asian markets, especially South Korea. He highlights hawkish Bank of Korea signals, robust exports and inflation, and expects South Korean rates to stay sticky.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD struggles to regain momentum below 50-day SMA
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) pulls back from intraday highs on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds amid lingering uncertainty over whether the United States and Iran can reach a deal to end the three-month-old war.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: US Dollar clears 50-day SMA as bulls target 0.7900
item.description: The USD/CHF pair edges modestly higher on Tuesday, gaining 0.21% as buyers test the current week’s high of 0.7884 after bouncing off daily lows of 0.7844.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Seen above 18,000 at end of 2026 against dollar – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research’s Philip Wee has revised higher his USD/IDR projections, now expecting the pair to end 2026 slightly above 18,000 versus 16,500 previously.

item.title: US President Trump signs order to gain early access to powerful AI models
item.description: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Tuesday aimed at giving the government early access to powerful new artificial intelligence (AI) models. Under the proposal, AI developers would voluntarily submit new models for government cybersecurity testing before their public release.

item.title: Gold: Bearish pattern caps tight consolidation – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank's strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret describe Gold trading in a tight consolidation around $4500/oz, forming the lower bound of a descending triangle pattern.

item.title: Gold holds near $4,500 as US-Iran talks halt, US Dollar recovers
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) advances a modest 0.16% on Tuesday as risk appetite improves after Israel and Hezbollah halted hostilities due to the intervention of US President Donald Trump. The XAU/USD pair trades near the $4,500 mark after bouncing off daily lows of $4,463.

item.title: Asia FX: Inflation and trade shifts shape KRW and IDR – BNY
item.description: BNY's Bob Savage flags continued KRW weakness despite stronger South Korean inflation, which supports a hawkish Bank of Korea (BoK) stance. In Indonesia, Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) data show fragile manufacturing, while inflation has moved above expectations even after a 50 bp rate hike.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Growth and AI flows anchor TWD – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank reports that USD/TWD traded steadily around 31.37, with realised one‑month volatility near 4.5%, lower than several regional peers.

item.title: United States Dollar Index recovers intraday losses as Middle East uncertainty lingers
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback’s value against a basket of six major currencies, rebounds on Tuesday as mixed signals surrounding US-Iran negotiations help the index recover earlier intraday losses.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Range trade persists against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/SGD stayed firm on Monday, closing around 1.2788 after trading between 1.2759 and 1.2803, supported by a stronger US Dollar and a stable Singapore Dollar (SGD) Nominal Effective Exchange Rate (NEER).
